exposure.title: What do you really risk without local representation?
exposure.p1: When you are not on site, you lose ongoing control over your home.
exposure.p2: Small problems do not make noise. They grow when no one checks.
exposure.p3: You find out about them when you are 1500 km away — without keys and without the ability to react immediately.
exposure.p4: A few days of delay is enough for a minor fault to become a serious cost.
exposure.close1: It is not about whether something will happen.
exposure.close2: It is that you will find out too late.

contrast.left2: You learn about a problem when someone notices it — not when it starts.
contrast.left3: Every situation begins with logistics: who can go, who has keys, who has time.
contrast.left4: You make decisions remotely, without the full picture.
contrast.left5: Contractors act, but there is no stable reference for the property's condition.
contrast.left6: Coordination responsibility stays on your side.

contrast.right1: The property is kept clean and prepared for your return or your guests.
contrast.right2: It's checked regularly on an agreed schedule.
contrast.right3: Its condition is documented and compared over time.
contrast.right4: Keys and access are on-site — no improvisation.
contrast.right5: When something happens, the response starts with action.
contrast.right6: Within the agreed limit, a decision can be made immediately.

water.title: A leak nobody sees can cost thousands.
water.body: When a property stands empty, water can spend weeks working into the floor, units, and walls before you see the damage on arrival.
water.responseLead: Sentinel reduces the time a problem is left alone.
water.responseBody: During local checks, we look for these signals, document them, and trigger the agreed action path before a small leak becomes major damage.
water.alt: A water mark and floor damage in an unchecked property.

moisture.title: Moisture in a closed property does not stay on the surface.
moisture.body: Near the sea, without regular ventilation, a small mark can move deeper into the wall. Then it is no longer cleaning — it is drying, mold removal, and costly repair.
moisture.responseLead: Sentinel checks the property between your stays.
moisture.responseBody: Ventilation, wall checks, and condition records help catch moisture earlier — before you return to smell, stains, and a problem that has grown.
moisture.alt: Moisture and early mold near an air-conditioning unit.

access.title: A contractor cannot help if nobody can open the door.
access.body: Keys, entry, checks, or preparation start depending on urgent calls from abroad and finding someone local at the last minute.
access.responseLead: Access is arranged before the problem appears.
access.responseBody: You decide remotely, while Sentinel opens, coordinates, and confirms local actions within the rules agreed in advance.
access.alt: Keys and access coordination for the property.

arrival.title: Your holiday should not become a week of sorting the property.
arrival.body: You come for a few days, but instead of resting you check defects, air the rooms, clean, look for a contractor, and chase things that could have started earlier.
arrival.responseLead: Part of the local work happens before you arrive.
arrival.responseBody: Checks, ventilation, cleaning, preparation, and coordination help you enter a property ready to use — not another list of problems.
arrival.alt: A bedroom not prepared for the owner's arrival.

turnover.title: Guests judge the result, not the preparation process.
turnover.body: They do not care who was meant to clean, place towels, or check the property. If the stay starts with gaps, the problem returns to the owner immediately.
turnover.responseLead: Turnover has an agreed local structure.
turnover.responseBody: Cleaning, preparation, and readiness checks can be coordinated before guest arrival, instead of depending on several people and urgent messages.
turnover.alt: A bedroom mid-turnover: bed linen, towels, and items to prepare before the next stay.

damage.title: Post-stay damage can disappear between messages.
damage.body: A stain, crack, or damaged item quickly becomes a dispute: when it happened, who saw it, and whether it can still be recorded before the next booking.
damage.responseBody: Visible damage and changes in the property can be checked, photographed, and passed on for decision before the issue reaches the next stay.
damage.alt: A stain on the sofa and a mark on the wooden table in the living room after a guest stay.

dispatcher.title: Between stays, the owner becomes the dispatcher.
dispatcher.body: Keys, technician entry, cleaning, corrections, and confirmations start depending on you — even when you are far away and only have your phone.
dispatcher.responseLead: Access and actions are agreed locally.
dispatcher.responseBody: Keys, entries, technicians, and preparation can follow agreed rules, without fresh improvisation between every stay.
dispatcher.alt: Keys, a phone, a door, and a technician's tool bag in the property entrance.

boiler.title: A failure during the stay becomes your problem immediately.
boiler.body: No hot water, a boiler error, or another basic fault does not wait. The guest expects a response, and the owner starts handling the situation remotely.
boiler.responseLead: The report has a local point of response.
boiler.responseBody: Sentinel can check the situation on site, confirm the scale of the problem, and activate the agreed path of action before the fault becomes a bigger guest conflict.
boiler.alt: A boiler panel showing a pressure gauge and a red error message during a guest stay.

wrongStartingAssumption.title: Misreading how the property will be used can distort the check rhythm and access rules.
wrongStartingAssumption.body: A property may begin as private-use and later receive guests. If the scope is chosen from an assumption, later needs become exceptions.
wrongStartingAssumption.responseLead: We first check how the property is actually used.
wrongStartingAssumption.responseBody: Sentinel separates private use, guest stays, and mixed use before scope, visit rhythm, and decision level are defined.
wrongStartingAssumption.alt: A bedroom prepared for both an owner stay and possible guest use.

prematureGuestSetup.title: Guest-support structure built too early starts running by itself.
prematureGuestSetup.body: Keys, towels, cleaning, and instructions appear before it is clear whether the property will actually operate around guest stays.
prematureGuestSetup.responseLead: We do not set guest procedure before the model is classified.
prematureGuestSetup.responseBody: First we check whether the property needs private-use, guest-stay, or mixed oversight. Only then do access, preparation, and documentation rules follow.
prematureGuestSetup.alt: A hallway with keys, towels, cleaning supplies, and an instruction board.

wrongScopeAssumption.title: A scope chosen from a guess rarely fits reality.
wrongScopeAssumption.body: Too little scope leaves gaps; too much starts work the property does not yet need. The mismatch appears when the first use pattern changes.
wrongScopeAssumption.responseLead: Scope follows the classified model, not a default category.
wrongScopeAssumption.responseBody: Sentinel structures stay frequency, access, cleaning, decisions, and reporting, then points to the correct operational intensity.
wrongScopeAssumption.alt: A table with a tablet, notes, keys, and a property scope plan.

adHocScopeCreep.title: Undefined scope quickly becomes a chain of exceptions.
adHocScopeCreep.body: Small requests for access, cleaning, repair, or preparation get added one by one. After a while, nobody knows what was agreed.
adHocScopeCreep.responseLead: The boundary between structure and one-off request is set in advance.
adHocScopeCreep.responseBody: Sentinel records what belongs inside the service, what needs a separate decision, and when the owner must approve work outside scope.
adHocScopeCreep.alt: A cupboard with keys, towels, cleaning supplies, and items added to property handling.

q1.question: Can I start immediately without full onboarding?
q1.answer: No. Service is activated only after complete onboarding. This protects both parties.

q2.question: What if I don't have all information yet?
q2.answer: Onboarding will pause until required information is provided. Service cannot begin with incomplete data.

q3.question: Can I change my package during onboarding?
q3.answer: Yes, before activation. After activation, package changes require new agreement.

q4.question: What if the initial inspection reveals problems?
q4.answer: Issues are documented in the initial report. Client decides whether to address them before service begins or accept property "as is" with documented baseline.

q5.question: Do I pay before or after activation?
q5.answer: Payment terms are specified during package confirmation (Step 2). Service activation may require initial payment or deposit as per agreed terms.

q6.question: Can someone else be present during initial inspection?
q6.answer: Yes, if arranged in advance. Not required.

q7.question: What if I need to delay activation after onboarding?
q7.answer: Discuss with Sentinel. If activation is delayed significantly after onboarding, a re-check may be required before service starts to confirm the baseline condition remains accurate.

q1.question: What exactly is Sentinel?
q1.answer: Sentinel is local owner representation: on-site presence, checks, coordination, and reports inside a defined package. It is not concierge, rental management, or open-ended help. If you need steady, clear structure in the service area, the model may fit.

q2.question: Can I order a single visit without a package?
q2.answer: No. Sentinel works through a monthly package because a consistent process, access, and full context matter. For a single visit, a local contractor is usually the better fit; Sentinel starts after package onboarding.

q3.question: What if I need something not in my package?
q3.answer: We can assess it separately. Work outside the package needs a clear request, quote, and approval before it is done. If the need repeats, a different package or add-on may fit better.

q4.question: Can you let in a cleaner or technician if I have Basic package?
q4.answer: Not in Basic. Cleaner, technician, or other third-party access coordination requires Extended or Full. With Basic, the owner arranges access separately.

q5.question: What exactly is an "access event"?
q5.answer: It is one controlled entry for a third party: travel, opening, presence or supervision, securing the property, and a short record. Visit length does not change the classification. Extended includes 2 access events per month; extra events are billed separately. Full covers access events within the confirmed package scope.

q6.question: Can I ask for entry "just for a moment"?
q6.answer: That still counts as an access event. Even a brief entry requires travel, coordination, opening, and securing the property. If this will happen often, choose a package with the right access scope.

operations.title: Operations & Scheduling
operations.description: Questions about visit timing, technician coordination, and operational windows.

q7.question: What if a technician arrives "between 9 AM and 2 PM"?
q7.answer: A long technician window needs to be planned in advance. Basic and Extended do not include hours of waiting on site. Full can include presence during service visits when it fits the agreed scope.

q8.question: Do you react immediately to every request?
q8.answer: No. Agreed response time (SLA) and decision timing are 48h, 24h, or same day depending on package. This does not guarantee repair time, because parts, contractors, and availability are not fully controlled by Sentinel.

emergencies.description: Questions about emergency response, decision-making authority, and financial limits.

q9.question: What is considered an emergency?
q9.answer: An emergency is an event that threatens property damage, loss, or safety: active leak, broken security, gas, electrical issue, fire damage. WiFi, guest comfort, and minor defects are not emergencies. Response depends on package scope and decision limits.

q10.question: What happens in emergency if I don't answer phone?
q10.answer: In the Full package, Sentinel may secure the property up to the agreed €300 limit. In Basic and Extended, every paid action requires the owner’s prior approval. Whatever the package, Sentinel documents the event.

q11.question: What is the decision limit in Full package?
q11.answer: The standard limit is €300 per single decision. During onboarding, it can be set at €500. Anything above the limit needs owner approval before action.

q12.question: Do you take financial responsibility for damages?
q12.answer: No. Sentinel coordinates action and represents the owner within agreed scope, but it does not replace insurance or guarantee that every incident will be prevented. The owner must keep suitable property insurance.

practical.title: Practical Operations
practical.description: Questions about day-to-day service details, visit frequency, and package changes.

q13.question: Can you store valuables?
q13.answer: Only by clear agreement and with items logged. Sentinel does not take responsibility for valuables that were not declared. High-value items should have their own insurance.

q14.question: Can you take care of animals?
q14.answer: Occasionally, if agreed in advance. Regular animal care is not part of Sentinel packages and usually needs a separate local service.

q15.question: Do you check utility meters?
q15.answer: Yes, if the meters are accessible. In Basic, the scope is agreed during onboarding; Extended and Full can include readings and photos. Format depends on package and property layout.

q16.question: Can I have only one visit per month?
q16.answer: The standard rhythm is 2 visits per month. A lower frequency can be discussed, but it increases time between checks and may limit the scope of checks and actions. It must be clearly agreed.

q17.question: Can I change my package during cooperation?
q17.answer: Yes, by mutual agreement. The new package and change date are confirmed in writing, usually from the next billing period.

q18.question: Do you support properties with regular guest stays?
q18.answer: Only inside an agreed module, not as rental management. Sentinel can cover preparation, access, cleaning, or post-departure checks. Bookings, pricing, guest communication, and running the rental business stay outside scope.

communication.title: Communication & Rules
communication.description: Questions about how to contact Sentinel, policy changes, and service refusal.

q19.question: How does communication work?
q19.answer: New inquiries use the form, email, or general number. Active clients receive a separate operational channel, usually phone/WhatsApp, while formal arrangements stay on email. The public form is not an emergency line; we do not work through private team numbers.

q20.question: Can you refuse cooperation?
q20.answer: Yes. Sentinel may decline if the property is outside the area, expectations do not fit the monthly packages, or service would not be workable. The service area is a fixed boundary, not a travel surcharge. This check happens before onboarding.

q21.question: Can prices and terms change?
q21.answer: Yes. Changes are announced in advance and do not apply retroactively. They start from the next billing period, and the client can accept the new terms or end service after the current period.

q22.question: What if something isn't described in the documentation?
q22.answer: If something is not listed, it is not automatically in the package. You can ask about it, but it needs separate review, approval, and pricing. Legal and regulatory compliance remains with the owner.

q23.question: Why are there so many rules?
q23.answer: Because clear scope protects service quality. The owner knows what to expect, and Sentinel can work consistently and responsibly. The rules are there to prevent misunderstandings, not to make contact harder.

q24.answer: They apply to the website, conversations, offers, agreements, and ongoing cooperation. Verbal exceptions do not replace agreed terms. If someone does not accept these rules, Sentinel is probably not the right service.

intro.description: Sentinel is a local property representation service operating on a package-based model with defined scope and documented procedures. This page explains our operational philosophy, geographic focus, system design, and the operational resources that support service delivery.
intro.subtext: We do not operate on personality-driven trust or concierge flexibility. We operate on documented procedures, defined scope, and enforceable accountability.

philosophy.title: Why Package-Based Property Representation
philosophy.intro: Sentinel was designed to solve a specific operational problem: property owners living outside Spain need reliable local representation, but traditional models—key holding, concierge services, or full property management—create misaligned expectations and undefined responsibility.
philosophy.subtitle: Package-based service model exists because:

scopeClarity.title: Scope clarity prevents disputes:
scopeClarity.description: When services are defined in advance, both parties know exactly what is included and what requires separate arrangement.

procedures.title: Documented procedures enable consistency:
procedures.description: Standardized checklists, inspection protocols, and reporting ensure service quality does not depend on individual discretion.

responsibility.title: Defined responsibility protects both parties:
responsibility.description: Clear boundaries prevent uncontrolled scope, unrealistic expectations, and actions outside the agreed model.

geographic.title: Geographic focus enables accountability:
geographic.description: Limiting service area to Torrevieja + 50-70km ensures realistic response times and sustainable service quality.

philosophy.practice: What this means in practice: If a service is not explicitly listed in your package, it is not included. This is not inflexibility—it is the foundation of reliable, accountable service delivery.

geographic.title: Geographic Boundary: Operational Rationale
geographic.intro: Sentinel services properties within Torrevieja and approximately 50-70km radius. This geographic limitation is permanent and applies to all clients without exception.
geographic.subtitle: Why geographic boundaries exist:

reasons.responseTime: Response timing: Full package includes same-day response within defined decision boundaries. This is only sustainable within manageable distance.
reasons.visitFrequency: Visit frequency reliability: Regular biweekly or weekly visits require proximity. Distant properties create scheduling conflicts and service degradation.
reasons.emergencyAccess: Emergency access capability: Property securing in case of active leaks, broken locks, or weather damage requires rapid physical presence.
reasons.qualityControl: Quality control: Local presence enables relationship management with cleaners, technicians, and municipal services. Distance erodes these operational relationships.
reasons.sustainability: Cost sustainability: Travel time beyond 70km makes service economically unsustainable without pricing that defeats the purpose.

geographic.footer: Properties outside this area cannot be serviced—not temporarily, not as exceptions, not at premium pricing. This boundary is designed to protect service quality for clients within the area, not to limit growth arbitrarily.

hero.headline: When you are away, someone local has to maintain continuity.
hero.lead: A property does not pause because its owner left. Keys, access, water, technicians, and decisions carry on — and someone on site has to keep the situation moving, not just complete isolated tasks. Sentinel is the local team that carries the next steps forward.
hero.boundaryCta: What Sentinel is — and is not
hero.photoAlt: Keys and an operational record prepared on a table before a property handover.
hero.photoCaption: Keys, operational record, handover — the working end of owner representation.

why.title: Remote ownership does not fail at cleaning. It fails when work stops after the first task.
why.body: Most owners can find someone to mop a floor or water the plants. What breaks is the chain around those tasks: who holds the keys, who lets the technician in, who decides at what cost, who writes down what was found — and who carries the next step forward. Sentinel was built so each of those steps leads to the next.

points.title: Nobody local carries the situation forward
points.body: Helpers each hold a piece — a key, a chore, a phone number. No one sees the work through from one step to the next.

points.title: Decisions drift
points.body: Without agreed limits, every small event becomes a message thread stretched across two countries.

points.title: Nothing is written down
points.body: Favors leave no record. When something goes wrong, there is no account of what was done, when, or why.

why.closing: Sentinel replaces informal delegation with one accountable local layer: agreed scope, controlled access, documented visits, bounded decisions.

accessBreak.alt: Access check at a property entrance.
accessBreak.caption: Access rules include locks and keys — they are not an add-on to cleaning.

contrast.title: Cleaning is a task. Oversight is a chain.
contrast.intro: Property oversight is a chain of access, decisions, timing, and documentation. A task can be hired out. Someone still has to connect the next steps and carry the situation through to a decision.

rows.body: The apartment is left in order. That is the whole job — and it should be.
The fault in front of them gets solved. The situation around it is not theirs to carry.
Access, timing, decisions, records, and escalation are coordinated on site within the agreed scope. You retain decision authority.

contrast.closing: Others do work at the property. Sentinel maintains continuity between those tasks.

team.title: A small local team, not casual help.
team.body: Sentinel is not a platform routing tasks to strangers. It works locally through a small operating team: coordination, access, documentation, property preparation, and field support. An owner is never passed to a random helper — every task lands inside an agreed operating structure.
team.named: Day to day, owner contact runs through Aleksy Gugała, Sentinel's named operating contact.
team.area: The team is based around Torrevieja and works within roughly 50–70 km of it — close enough for presence to stay real.
team.photoAlt: The Sentinel local team at a property entrance.
team.photoCaption: The Sentinel local team. Work stays inside agreed scope and decision limits.

boundary.title: What Sentinel is, and what it is not.
boundary.intro: Sentinel gives the owner on-site presence, records, and coordination of agreed actions. When your decision is needed, we ask rather than act on our own. We do not replace the owner, a rental agency, or a contractor.

isItems.title: On-site presence
isItems.body: A local person checks condition, access, and events — inside agreed limits.

isItems.title: Documented actions
isItems.body: Condition, actions, and decisions are documented, not remembered.

isItems.title: Owner approval
isItems.body: It is clear when your approval is needed, based on scope, cost, and responsibility.

isItems.title: Agreed coordination
isItems.body: We coordinate technicians, cleaning, and access only within the agreed scope.

isItems.title: Ask before acting
isItems.body: When action exceeds the package, limit, or authority, we ask the owner to decide.

isNotItems.title: A concierge
isNotItems.body: Personal errands and open-ended favors are not the service.

isNotItems.title: A rental agency
isNotItems.body: Bookings, pricing, licensing, and guest platforms stay with the owner.

isNotItems.title: A contractor
isNotItems.body: Sentinel coordinates work; it does not build, and it does not own third-party quality.

isNotItems.title: An unlimited hotline
isNotItems.body: Response follows the package, agreed limits, and contractor availability.

isNotItems.title: A favor network
isNotItems.body: Every action has a scope, a record, and a named responsibility.

sections.title: 1. Definition of Service
sections.body:
Sentinel provides a package-based local property representation service within a defined operational scope.

The service is not:

Insurance
A concierge service
A rental agency
A general contractor
Full-scope property management

sections.title: 2. Geographic Area
sections.body:
The service is provided only within Torrevieja and a 50–70 km radius.

Properties outside this area cannot be served.

sections.title: 3. Package Model
sections.body:
Services are delivered only under monthly packages:

Basic
Extended
Full

If a service is not explicitly listed in the package, it is not included.

Additional services require separate agreement and quotation.

sections.title: 4. SLA
sections.body:
SLA defines:

Response time
Decision time

SLA does not guarantee time to full resolution of an issue.

sections.title: 5. Decision Authority
sections.body:
In the Full Package a decision limit applies:

Standard: €300 per single decision
Optional: €500 (if agreed)

Decisions above the limit require owner approval.

sections.title: 6. Liability
sections.body:
Sentinel is responsible for:

Delivery of services in accordance with the package
Documentation of actions
Response in line with SLA

Sentinel is not responsible for:

Force majeure
Errors by third-party contractors
Insurance-type losses
Failure to prevent all incidents

sections.title: 7. Payments
sections.body:
The service is billed:

Monthly in advance
Minimum engagement period: 3 months

Payment may be made by:

Bank transfer
Online via the payment system

Non-payment may result in suspension or termination of the service.

sections.title: 8. Termination
sections.body:
The client may terminate the service at the end of the billing period.

Sentinel may terminate the service in case of:

Breach of scope
Non-payment
Operational impossibility
Conduct that prevents safe delivery of the service

sections.title: 9. Package Changes
sections.body:
A package change requires:

Mutual agreement
Written documentation

Changes do not apply retroactively.

sections.title: 10. Jurisdiction
sections.body:
These terms are governed by the law of Spain.

Disputes are resolved by the competent courts.

sections.title: 1. Data Controller
sections.body:
The data controller is Sentinel, a local property representation service operating in Torrevieja and within a 50–70 km radius.

Contact for data protection matters:
Email: sentinelcostablanca@gmail.com

sections.title: 2. Scope of Data Processed
sections.body:
Sentinel processes only data necessary for:

Responding to enquiries sent via the contact form
Conclusion and performance of the package agreement
Invoicing
Online payment processing
Operational communication with the client

Data may include:

Name
Email address
Phone number
Property location
Billing details
Information required in the service onboarding process

Sentinel does not process data for marketing purposes without explicit consent.

sections.title: 3. Legal Basis for Processing
sections.body:
Data is processed on the basis of:

Performance of contract or pre-contractual steps
Legal obligations (e.g. accounting)
Legitimate interest of the controller (operational communication)
User consent (where applicable)

sections.title: 4. Data Retention
sections.body:
Data is retained:

For the duration of the engagement
For periods required by law (e.g. accounting records)
Until withdrawal of consent, where processing is based on consent

After the required periods, data is deleted or anonymised.

sections.title: 5. Online Payments
sections.body:
For online payments, transaction data is processed by external payment service providers.

Sentinel does not store full payment card data.

Payment providers act as independent data controllers under their own terms.

sections.title: 6. Cookies
sections.body:
The site may use:

Technical cookies (necessary for the site to function)
Functional cookies
Analytics cookies (if enabled)

Users may manage cookies via browser settings.

Disabling some cookies may affect site functionality.

sections.title: 7. User Rights
sections.body:
Users have the right to:

Access their data
Rectification of data
Erasure of data
Restriction of processing
Data portability
Object to processing
Withdraw consent at any time

Requests should be sent to the controller's email address.

sections.title: 8. Data Sharing
sections.body:
Data may be disclosed to:

Accounting service providers
Payment providers
Technology partners operating the site infrastructure

Data is not sold or shared for marketing purposes.

sections.title: 9. Security
sections.body: Sentinel applies appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect data against unauthorised access, loss or disclosure.

sections.title: 10. Policy Changes
sections.body: The Privacy Policy may be updated following legal or operational changes. The current version is published on the site.
